class.name: TerrainMaterial
class.brief_description: How a [Terrain3D]'s layers are blended into a surface.
class.description: The shading settings for a terrain, separate from its [TerrainData] because they are a matter of taste rather than of any one terrain: save one as a resource and share it between every terrain in a game.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], ground steeper than [member auto_slope_angle] shows [member auto_slope_layer] whatever is painted there, so cliffs look like rock without painting them. [method Terrain3D.get_surface_name] takes it into account.
The slope in degrees at which [member auto_slope_layer] takes over.
The range of slopes in degrees, centred on [member auto_slope_angle], over which [member auto_slope_layer] fades in.
The index of the layer shown on steep ground. Enabling [member TerrainLayer.triplanar] on it keeps its texture from stretching on cliffs.
How sharply layers give way to each other when [member height_blending] is on. Lower values give crisper edges.

If [code]true[/code], where layers overlap the one whose height (the alpha channel of its [member TerrainLayer.albedo_texture]) stands taller shows through, instead of the layers simply fading into each other.
How strongly the ground's brightness varies over large distances, which hides the repetition of the textures from far away.
The size in metres of the patches of [member macro_variation].
How much darker painted wetness makes the ground, from [code]0.0[/code] for none to [code]1.0[/code] for black. Wet ground is also made glossy and smoothed over, the way water fills small bumps.
